title: Semantius translation work file
description: What one language still needs, in one file, for a translator (usually an agent) to fill in. Written by apps/web/scripts/i18n/translate.mjs into i18n/ at the repository root, beside the language file it is about, and read back by import.mjs. It is COMMITTED: a partly filled one is half-finished work, and regenerating it hands back empty strings. Every entry carries its English source; `translation` is the only field to edit. The ICU placeholders a translation must keep are read off the source TEXT by import.mjs, on both sides, and are deliberately not a field here: an expectation stored in the file the translator edits can be emptied, and the entry it then stops checking is the one hiding a dropped placeholder.

locale.description: The catalog language being translated, e.g. de-DE.

generated.description: When the file was produced. Informational.

entries.description: The work: one entry per key in the index that the language has no translation for.

key.description: The stored key. For a code string, the English source text itself (a disambiguated one is prefixed, `columnVisibility.View`); for model text, the model path under `module.`; for a server error, its code.

source.description: The English (or, for a server sentence, the original) text to translate.

translation.description: FILL THIS IN. Empty means still untranslated; import.mjs skips it.

comment.description: A note the developer left for the translator.

hints.description: What each OTHER managed language already says for this key, by BCP-47 tag (MANAGED_LANGUAGES in scripts/i18n/extract.mjs). CONTEXT ONLY — import.mjs never reads it. English underspecifies: `Order` is an entity in nwind and a sort position in `order_column`, and a reviewed language has already had to decide which. What the sources agree on is the meaning; where they differ is language-specific packaging. A language with no translation for the key is omitted rather than offered as an empty string, and the whole field is absent when no managed language has one.
